title: Middle East standoff: Why Gulf states may accept that Iran will control Hormuz
content: Gulf energy producers have acknowledged Iran's assertion of control over the critical Strait of Hormuz. This development occurs amidst attempts to resume passage through this essential route, which are stymied by ongoing tensions. Governments in the region prioritize peace over export delays, while Iran aims for financial easing and a prohibition of international warships, extending the disruption of global energy channels.

title: Old allies, new equation? Why SAD and BJP may join hands for Punjab polls
content: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini has categorically denied any prospective alliance with Shiromani Akali Dal for 2027 Punjab assembly elections. However, recent discussions between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and SAD leader Sukhbir Singh Badal have led to renewed speculation around possible tie-up. After the meeting, SAD, whose electoral fortunes have waned significantly, changed its perspective on delimitation. The BJP is reportedly keen on dominating any potential alliance.

title: Trump's Turkey takeout: World's most protected man spirited out in catering container
content: In a covert operation to ensure President Trump's safety, his security team reportedly employed a catering vehicle to transport him from a decoy aircraft in Turkey, responding to credible Iranian threats. This complex plan involved a smaller airplane ferrying him to Britain while a decoy remained in view, highlighting the ongoing challenges of protecting a president using foreign-supplied aircraft.

title: Why Messi didn't visit Kerala? Sports department tells govt in 'highly confidential manner'
content: Kerala’s Sports Department has submitted a confidential inquiry report into the failed proposal to bring Lionel Messi and Argentina’s football team to the state. The probe examined whether proper procedures and agreements were followed. While reports suggest serious findings, Sports Minister O J Janeesh withheld details. Former minister V Abdurahiman rejected allegations, saying the government suffered no financial loss.

title: 70 dead, 204 roads blocked: Himachal reels under monsoon fury; damage tops Rs 910 cr
content: Himachal Pradesh has been severely affected by monsoon rains, resulting in 70 fatalities and 204 roadblocks. Damages to public property have skyrocketed to over Rs 910 crore. The primary causes of these tragic deaths include landslides and mishaps from steep terrains. Additionally, 93 lives were lost due to road accidents during this challenging period. Restoration efforts are ongoing but are significantly hindered by continuous rain, creating additional hazards.

title: August 12 solar eclipse: Europe set for first total eclipse in 27 years
content: Europe will witness its first total solar eclipse in twenty-seven years on August twelfth.  Millions across Iceland and northern Spain will experience this rare celestial event.  Nasa will livestream the eclipse for viewers outside the path of totality.  Americans will see a partial eclipse, while Canada also observes it.  This eclipse begins an unusual period of significant celestial occurrences.

title: Mark Zuckerberg's $300M yacht booed over rescue call; clarification issued
content: Mark Zuckerberg's superyacht Launchpad faced criticism after a stranded boat incident. The vessel's crew was reportedly on a different radio channel during the emergency. Help was already en route when the yacht's crew reviewed the assistance request. The yacht, valued at $390 million, was closer to the distressed skiff. Passengers on a nearby cruise ship booed the yacht's perceived inaction.

title: This day in space: NASA launched first communications satellite in 1960
content: On August 12, 1960, NASA launched Echo 1A, a 100-foot balloon that became its first successful communications satellite. The passive spacecraft reflected telephone, radio and television signals between distant points on Earth. It also helped NASA study atmospheric density, solar pressure and satellite triangulation before re-entering Earth’s atmosphere in 1968.

title: Missouri plant turns old wind turbine blades into cement feedstock
content: Repurposing decommissioned wind turbine blades is becoming a promising trend, moving away from traditional landfill disposal. These large fiberglass structures are now being shredded and incorporated into cement production. Furthermore, innovative designs have led to the transformation of some blades into pedestrian bridges. While these initiatives are commendable, they signal just the beginning.

title: Accenture CEO Julie Sweet makes an 'August request' to employees
content: Accenture has implemented a new policy allowing employees to carry over their unused vacation days, aiming to bolster business performance as the fiscal year winds down. CEO Julie Sweet has urged employees to maximize their efforts in these critical weeks. However, this adjustment may inadvertently dissuade workers from taking necessary breaks, raising concerns among investors following a decline in new bookings.

title: Shweta Tiwari diagnosed with dengue, hospitalised
content: Shweta Tiwari, the popular actress renowned for her performances in shows like Kasautii Zindagii Kay, has been hospitalized due to dengue fever. As she undergoes treatment, she remains focused on her upcoming appearance in The Traitors 2. Meanwhile, her ex-husband Raja Chaudhary has made several allegations concerning her past relationships, which are stirring public interest amidst her health struggles.

title: After being denied a direct spot, how can Windies qualify for the 2027 WC?
content: West Indies, two-time ODI World Cup champions, will miss out on direct qualification for the 2027 tournament and must go through the Qualifier in February. Winning it secures direct entry to the second round, while finishing second to fourth means another hurdle. Having missed the 2023 World Cup and 2025 Champions Trophy, the Caribbean side cannot afford another setback.

title: UK radio station falsely announces King Charles’ death, breaches standards
content: King Charles’ death was mistakenly announced on UK radio station Radio Caroline after a staff member accidentally aired pre-recorded statements prepared for such an event. The broadcast included the national anthem and 16 minutes of silence before regular programming resumed. Ofcom ruled that the station breached broadcast standards over the inaccurate report and delayed correction.

title: Jaguar TCS Racing sets world record with 29 runners over 100km
content: Jaguar TCS Racing has marked the end of the Formula E GEN3 era in a unique way. Ahead of the London E-Prix, 29 runners from Jaguar TCS Racing and Tata Consultancy Services covered more than 100km across London to create a GPS drawing of the Jaguar I-TYPE 7. The effort helped the team set a Guinness World Record before its home season finale.

title: Undertaker and Michelle McCool’s combined net worth in 2026
content: The Undertaker and Michelle McCool maintain significant wealth through various post-wrestling ventures.  Their combined net worth is estimated between 21-22.5 million dollars in 2026.  The Undertaker's legendary WWE career and ongoing media work contribute substantially to his fortune.  Michelle McCool also leverages her wrestling legacy for continued commercial opportunities and income.  Their financial success demonstrates enduring value from wrestling careers even after retirement.

title: Patrick Mahomes’ controversial confession sparks fitness debate ahead of new season
content: Patrick Mahomes' recent confesion about his wealth has sparked a massive debate about his fitness as many remain worried about him.

title: HC rules in the favour of Janhvi, orders removal of obscene content from 5000 pages
content: The Delhi High Court has ordered removal of some online content targeting Janhvi Kapoor.  The court clarified that personality rights cannot be broadly applied to restrict expression.  It asked Kapoor's lawyers to narrow down unlawful content claims for action.  Blanket removal requests for fan pages and dynamic injunctions were rejected by the judge.  The case aims to bring clarity to celebrity personality rights in the digital age.

title: Lionel Messi steps away from football after father's death, no return date yet

title: Delhi slum rehab: How Bill in Assembly may bring more settlements into redevelopment net
content: The Delhi government is set to enhance rehabilitation efforts for jhuggi-jhopri settlements by shifting the eligibility cut-off date from 2006 to 2025, enabling additional clusters to qualify. This regulation encourages private firms and cooperatives to engage in redevelopment initiatives, while the Delhi Urban Shelter Improvement Board oversees the relocation and upgrading processes. Residents may also have a chance to financially support their new housing costs.

title: ‘Drama at this age is embarrassing’: Trisha's cryptic posts after Udhayanidhi row
content: Actor Trisha Krishnan returned to social media with cryptic posts after a controversy. Her posts followed alleged remarks by Udhayanidhi Stalin at a protest meeting. Police registered a case against Udhayanidhi, who was later released on station bail. Trisha's mother also shared a similar cryptic message on her Instagram. The posts have sparked speculation on social media platforms.

title: Duan Jansen, Marco’s twin brother, earns maiden South Africa call-up for Namibia tour
content: Duan Jansen, twin brother of Marco, has received his maiden South Africa call-up for the Namibia tour. The Proteas will play a T20I tri-series against Namibia and Zimbabwe before a historic three-match ODI series against Namibia. Bjorn Fortuin will captain the squad, while several domestic performers have earned opportunities to strengthen South Africa’s international depth.

title: Fitch retains India’s credit rating at BBB-, sees strong economy
content: The ratings agency said the Indian economy continues to demonstrate resilience despite the energy shock arising from the conflict in West Asia, supported by a strong growth outlook and sound external financing fundamentals.

title: 'Gruesome assault': High court denies bail to Olympic medallist in murder case
content: Justice Purushaindra Kumar dismissed Kumar's bail plea on August 6, citing concerns about his ability to influence witnesses, his conduct before his arrest, the seriousness of the alleged offence and his ability to affect the outcome of the ongoing trial.

title: Gangs of WhatsAppur: Mumbai’s thieves reinvent codes for digital age
content: Mumbai police have made headlines by unearthing a pickpocketing ring that relied on encrypted WhatsApp chats for coordination. This gang demonstrated intricate organization, defining roles and modifying their communication codes daily. Historically, thieves adapted hand signals and glances to avoid capture, yet this contemporary approach shows how technology is reshaping criminal tactics, enabling faster and safer exchanges.

title: Retirement homes get regulatory push: What buyers and senior citizens should know
content: In light of new safety regulations introduced by the Centre, retirement homes are set to undergo heightened scrutiny. Each state and Union Territory will embrace these policies designed for senior living facilities. Key aspects of the guidelines include RERA registration and the establishment of senior-friendly infrastructures. Developers will be required to follow these updated rules, reinforcing the regulatory framework governing this burgeoning housing market.

title: Direct tax collections rise sharply to Rs 8.11 lakh crore; non-corporate taxes lead
content: India's direct tax collections have surged impressively, seeing an increase of over twenty-three percent. As of August 10, gross direct tax collections reached a staggering Rs 9.55 lakh crore. The bulk of these collections stemmed from non-corporate tax receipts, while both corporate tax collections and Securities Transaction Tax experienced notable year-on-year growth. Nevertheless, government-issued refunds only saw a slight uptick during this period.

title: Pune conversion case: UK-based OCI holder booked under new Maharashtra law
content: Pune Police registered an FIR against a UK OCI cardholder for alleged religious conversion attempts.  The accused allegedly spoke about Jesus and made statements about Hindu deities.  In a separate case, a 21-year-old man was arrested under the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act.  This development follows a wider debate over religious conversion and foreign funding.  Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis stated that transparent organizations have nothing to fear.

title: Suriya reveals why his 1,700 sq ft Mumbai home feels better than Chennai bungalow
content: Actor Suriya enjoys the intimate charm of his 1700 sq ft home in Mumbai, a space filled with warmth and comfort. The couple moved here to reinforce family ties with Jyotika's parents during the pandemic. Their transition underscores the significance of family in challenging times. Don't miss Suriya's upcoming film 'Vishwanath and Sons,' releasing on August 14.

title: IPL cricketer Abishek Porel arrested on rape charge; woman alleges promise of marriage
content: Bengal Police arrested cricketer Abishek Porel on Tuesday in connection with a rape case.  The arrest followed a directive from the Calcutta High Court regarding the complaint.  A medical student alleged a physical relationship on the promise of marriage.  The complaint also includes charges of criminal intimidation and recording intimate moments.  Porel's career is now overshadowed by these ongoing legal proceedings.

title: UPI MDR: What is being proposed, and who pays the final cost? Explained
content: The government has clarified that UPI will continue to remain free for consumers and no transaction charges will be applicable to person-to-person payments. The government has also said that if an MDR is introduced in the future it will only be applicable to a limited category of merchant transactions.

title: Speeding BMW runs over woman in Delhi, villagers block road near T-3 terminal
content: A 48-year-old house help was killed by a speeding BMW car in Delhi. The driver, identified as Deepak, was apprehended by police officials after the incident. Angry locals blocked a road in protest, disrupting traffic movement near the airport. The victim's family expressed their desire for justice and strict action against the driver. Authorities have registered a case and initiated legal proceedings against the apprehended driver.

content: Maya Angelou’s insights emphasize that emotions are powerful and influential. Our words and deeds leave a significant emotional mark on those we encounter. By practicing kindness and showing empathy, we cultivate meaningful relationships in our daily lives. Aiming to be considerate allows us to leave others with positive feelings, ultimately shaping our interactions and enriching our experiences.

title: 'Discontent answered with bullets': MEA slams Pakistan over PoK crackdown

The Joint Awami Action Committee, prohibited from operating, led rallies demanding a fair distribution of refugee seats. Additionally, upcoming elections in the region were marred by violence and claims of electoral fraud, prompting India to call on the global community to hold Pakistan accountable for these violations.

title: US influencer faces action in Australia after picking up baby wombat for viral reel

Wildlife professionals cautioned against the dangers of interacting with wild creatures for social media fame. This event underscores a crucial message about respecting Australia's native wildlife, urging travelers to admire wombats from a safe distance without direct contact.

title: 'Eetha' New Release Date: Shraddha and Laxman Utekar film moves to December 4
